subject: Connector API contract: adaptor shim & 9-month stability proposal
messages:
From: Andrew Lim <andrew.lim@catalyst.io>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Cc: partners@catalyst.io
Date: Mon, 6 Jul 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Connector contract: request for stable header + compatibility window

Hi Jonas,

Thanks again for the demo last week — Catalyst's engineering team is ready to move our connector into production, but we hit a roadblock around two things that are blockers for our customers:

1) Contract stability: we rely on a small header/resolver handshake that your hosted runtime currently changes across minor releases. We need a clear guarantee or a stable header (suggest: X-Redwood-Connector-Version) so our adaptors can gracefully reject incompatible changes.

2) Deprecation window: a 6–12 month guarantee on minor changes would allow our ISV customers to certify and ship. Right now the rolling changes make certs brittle.

Attached is a short spec (catalyst_connector_spec_v1.pdf) showing how we use the header and a sample failure case. We’d like Redwood to consider two mechanical changes: (a) add the optional X-Redwood-Connector-Version header that echoing services can return; (b) ship a tiny compatibility shim we can insert client-side to map old header names to the new one as you roll forward.

Can you confirm if the platform team can entertain adding the header and a 9-month compatibility commitment? If not, what alternate mitigation would you propose? We’re targeting a production freeze on Aug 15 so time is tight.

Appreciate any guidance.

—Andrew
Andrew Lim
Director, Partnerships | Catalyst Integrations
attachments: catalyst_connector_spec_v1.pdf
From: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
To: Andrew Lim <andrew.lim@catalyst.io>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, priyom_das@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 6 Jul 2026 18:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Connector contract: request for stable header + compatibility window

Andrew — thanks for the clear ask and the spec, that helps. Quick read: reasonable and we should be able to support this without a major runtime refactor.

Proposed immediate plan:
- Short-term (next 2 weeks): implement optional X-Redwood-Connector-Version header at the gateway layer and add a compatibility shim artifact (a small mapping utility) that Catalyst can include client-side. We'll ship the shim as a tiny diff and a Docker image.
- Mid-term (30–90 days): formalize a compatibility policy for minor releases (propose 9 months), include deprecation warnings in responses and in the release notes, and add a CLI check for connector compatibility.
- Rollout: canary the header on a subset of backends and route Catalyst traffic through the canary once the shim is validated.

Marissa — can you confirm implementation effort estimates for the gateway header + shim and whether we can scope an initial canary by 7/20? Priyom — I’ve CC’d you to track partner comms and commercial ask for a 9-month stability commitment.

Andrew — we’ll follow up with a concrete timeline by EOD tomorrow.

Thanks,
Jonas
Jonas Weber
Head of Partnerships, Redwood Inference
From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Cc: Andrew Lim <andrew.lim@catalyst.io>, priyom_das@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 7 Jul 2026 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Connector contract: request for stable header + compatibility window

Jonas / Andrew — quick engineering note from the runtime team:

- Gateway header: trivial change in the edge layer. We can add X-Redwood-Connector-Version as an opt-in header emitted on responses and request echoes; effort estimate ~2 dev days including tests and metrics.
- Shim: we can produce a small Node/Go mapping tool that normalizes older header names (e.g., X-RW-Conn-Ver, X-RW-Version) into the new header. Will also add a liveness check endpoint that returns current supported versions. Estimate ~3 dev days including packaging and a Docker image.
- Canary: we can flip a feature flag and route 5% of Catalyst traffic to the canary. Recommend we also emit a 428 warning header for deprecated header names for the next 30 days to prompt update.

Open questions:
- Is Catalyst ok with a client-side shim instead of server-side backward compatibility? If not, we can add a server-side compat layer but that increases maintenance surface.
- Does Catalyst need an SLA-level written guarantee for the 9-month stability (legal/commercial)? Priyom, please advise.

I’ll prepare a minimal PR and an accompanying diff (redwood_compat_shim_proposal.diff) by EOD.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Software Engineer, Runtime
attachments: redwood_compat_shim_proposal.diff
From: Andrew Lim <andrew.lim@catalyst.io>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 7 Jul 2026 11:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Connector contract: request for stable header + compatibility window

Thanks Marissa — that sounds great and aligns with our constraints. Quick answers to your open questions:
- Client-side shim is acceptable for our customers as long as it’s officially published and versioned by Redwood (we don’t want to maintain forks).
- We will ask our procurement/legal team for a written commitment if Redwood can include a 9-month deprecation window as part of the Partner Addendum. That will likely be a lightweight clause and not a full SLA.

Two asks to keep this on schedule:
1) Can Redwood publish the shim artifact (Docker + npm) and a one-page install guide by 7/17?
2) Can you enable the canary routing for our test tenant on 7/20 so we can run compatibility tests?

If you can commit to those dates we’ll lock our production freeze for Aug 15 and route customers through the shim.

—Andrew
From: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
To: priyom_das@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 8 Jul 2026 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: Catalyst adaptor timeline and commercial ask

Priyom — summarizing next steps and owners (internal):
- Marissa: ship initial PR for header + shim artifact by 7/17 (Node + Docker + docs). Confirmed estimate 2–3 dev days. Attachments: redwood_compat_shim_proposal.diff, timeline_board.png.
- Ops: enable 5% canary routing for Catalyst test tenant on 7/20 (coordinate with infra on feature flag).
- Partnerships (me): draft Partner Addendum language for a 9-month deprecation window and share with Catalyst for review; escalate to legal if Catalyst requires formal contract language.
- Customer ask: publish artifacts (npm + docker) and one-page install guide by 7/17; confirm canary on 7/20.

I’ll follow up with Andrew after Marissa’s PR lands and once Ops confirms the canary. If procurement pushes for tighter contractual SLAs we’ll loop in legal.

Jonas
Head of Partnerships
Redwood Inference
